survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Compass Brief uses TIMSS 2019 eighth-grade data across multiple participating countries to compute cyberbullying and traditional bullying scales and to report country-level correlations with mathematics achievement. The manuscript describes scale construction and correlation analyses but does not report any use of TIMSS sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the analysis. Because the study focuses on descriptive/correlation-based relationships rather than training predictive ML models, the weighting strategy is not documented; therefore, it is unclear whether complex survey design features were incorporated. The only explicit sample restriction mentioned is excluding Kazakhstan due to unresolvable translation issues for the bullying questions; no other filtering rules are specified.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables in this brief are (i) cyberbullying and traditional bullying scales derived from TIMSS 2019 bullying items and (ii) mathematics achievement correlations reported at the country level. The manuscript does not describe plausible-value (PV) generation/combining or whether achievement was handled via PVs, WLE, or IRT theta; it also does not document any missing-data procedure for the achievement or bullying scales. Given the paper’s focus on correlation patterns rather than an explicit PV-based modeling workflow, the PV handling and missing-data strategy are not transparently reported, representing a methodological reporting gap.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TIMSS 2019 eighth-grade data from all participating countries for the cyberbullying/traditional bullying scale construction and correlation analyses, except Kazakhstan, which was excluded due to unresolvable data issues related to translation of the bullying questions. For item-level frequency tables and gender comparisons, the manuscript combines the first two response categories (“At least once a week” and “Once or twice a month”). For the mathematics achievement correlations, the brief reports that Israel had all missing data for one or more items in the online bullying scale, so the score was not estimated for that country.

data.outcome_summary: This IEA Compass Brief uses TIMSS 2019 eighth-grade data to study cyberbullying and its association with traditional bullying and mathematics achievement. Cyberbullying (from three cyberbullying-specific items) and traditional bullying scales are strongly correlated on average across educational systems (average r=0.65), with higher correlations in several countries (e.g., UAE (Abu Dhabi) r=0.80). For mathematics achievement, the brief reports negative country-level correlations between cyberbullying and eighth-grade mathematics, with the strongest negative relationships in systems such as UAE (Abu Dhabi) and South Africa; effect sizes are mostly medium-to-small (below 0.20). Gender-stratified results indicate that the cyberbullying–mathematics relationship is generally stronger for boys than girls. The manuscript does not report an explicit ML modeling pipeline, plausible-value handling, or a missing-data procedure, so the results should be interpreted as correlation-based descriptive evidence rather than causal estimates.
